title: Warning Against Adultery
overview: Proverbs Chapter 5 offers a father’s earnest counsel to his son, warning against the seductive dangers of adultery and the allure of the 'strange woman.' The chapter contrasts the deceptive sweetness of sin with its bitter consequences, urging faithfulness to one’s spouse and the pursuit of wisdom and discretion. It highlights the destructive outcomes of unfaithfulness, including loss of honor, wealth, and ultimately life itself. This chapter fits within Proverbs’ broader wisdom literature by emphasizing moral integrity, the fear of the Lord, and the practical benefits of obedience to divine instruction.
structure:
**Verses 1-6: The Warning Against the Strange Woman.** The chapter opens with a direct appeal to listen to wisdom and understanding, describing the seductive but deadly nature of the adulterous woman whose words are sweet yet lead to bitter ends.

**Verses 7-14: The Call to Avoid Her and the Consequences of Ignoring Wisdom.** The father urges his son to distance himself from the adulteress to preserve honor and life, warning of regret and sorrow that come from despising instruction and falling into folly.

**Verses 15-20: The Celebration of Marital Fidelity.** The text shifts to positive exhortation, encouraging the son to find satisfaction and joy in his own wife, portraying marital love as a blessed and exclusive fountain.

**Verses 21-23: The Divine Oversight and Judgment of Sin.** The chapter concludes by affirming that God watches all human ways and that sin ensnares the wicked, leading to death and ruin without correction.

keyVerses.text: For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights the deceptive allure of sin, emphasizing how temptation often appears sweet and attractive but conceals deadly consequences. It sets the tone for the chapter’s warning against adultery.

keyVerses.text: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:
keyVerses.significance: A clear command to avoid temptation altogether, this verse underscores the wisdom of proactive separation from sin’s occasions, illustrating the practical outworking of wisdom in daily life.

keyVerses.text: Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.
keyVerses.significance: This verse celebrates the joy and blessing of marital faithfulness, contrasting the earlier warnings with a positive vision of God-ordained love and satisfaction within marriage.

keyVerses.text: For the ways of man are before the eyes of the LORD, and he pondereth all his goings.
keyVerses.significance: This verse affirms God’s omniscient oversight of human behavior, reinforcing the accountability of every action and the certainty of divine judgment.

keyVerses.text: He shall die without instruction; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.
keyVerses.significance: The chapter closes with a sobering reminder of the fatal consequences of rejecting wisdom and instruction, emphasizing the spiritual and physical ruin that follows persistent folly.

characters.name: The Father
characters.description: The speaker who imparts wisdom and instruction to his son, warning him about the dangers of adultery and urging him to embrace discretion and faithfulness.

characters.name: The Son
characters.description: The recipient of the father’s wisdom, representing the reader or believer who is exhorted to heed instruction and avoid temptation.

characters.name: The Strange Woman
characters.description: A symbol of temptation and sin, representing adultery and immoral seduction that leads to destruction and death.

characters.name: The Wife of Thy Youth
characters.description: Represents marital faithfulness and the blessing of exclusive, loving relationship within marriage, contrasting the destructive allure of the adulteress.

characters.name: The LORD
characters.description: God, who watches over all human actions and holds sinners accountable, ensuring that folly and sin lead to judgment.

themes.description: The chapter emphasizes the necessity of listening to wisdom and instruction to avoid destructive sin, highlighting the biblical principle that knowledge and discretion protect from folly.
Adultery is portrayed as deceptively sweet but ultimately bitter and deadly, illustrating the biblical condemnation of sexual immorality and its consequences.
Faithfulness to one’s spouse is presented as a source of joy and blessing, reflecting God’s design for marriage as a covenant relationship.
God’s awareness of all human actions and His righteous judgment upon sin are affirmed, reinforcing accountability before the Lord.

historicalContext: Proverbs was written in ancient Israel, traditionally attributed to Solomon in the 10th century BC. The cultural context includes a patriarchal society where family honor and sexual purity were highly valued. Adultery was not only a moral offense but also a social and legal violation with severe consequences. The imagery of the 'strange woman' reflects common wisdom literature motifs warning young men against sexual immorality. Politically, Israel was a theocratic monarchy where wisdom teachings reinforced social order and covenant faithfulness to God. The emphasis on marital fidelity aligns with the broader biblical ethic promoting covenant loyalty and the sanctity of marriage.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology sees this chapter as emphasizing the sovereignty of God over human actions and the necessity of covenant faithfulness. The warnings against adultery are understood as calls to holiness and obedience to God’s moral law, with the consequences illustrating the just judgment of God on sin.

Dispensational interpreters highlight the practical wisdom for the believer in the present age, focusing on personal responsibility to avoid temptation and maintain purity. The chapter is seen as part of God’s timeless moral standards applicable across dispensations.

Early church fathers often allegorized the 'strange woman' as representing false teachings or idolatry, warning believers to remain faithful to Christ, the 'Bridegroom.' They emphasized the spiritual dangers of unfaithfulness and the need for vigilance in the Christian life.

crossReferences.connection: Affirms the honor of marriage and warns against sexual immorality, echoing Proverbs 5’s call to marital faithfulness.
Commands fleeing sexual immorality, paralleling the admonition to avoid the adulterous woman.
Describes temptation’s progression leading to sin and death, resonating with the chapter’s depiction of sin’s bitter end.
Speaks of God’s watchful eye over the righteous and the wicked, similar to Proverbs 5:21’s emphasis on divine oversight.
Exhorts husbands to love their wives as Christ loves the church, reinforcing the chapter’s celebration of marital love.

application: Guard your heart by avoiding situations and influences that lead to temptation, practicing proactive separation from sin.
Cultivate a joyful and exclusive relationship with your spouse, cherishing the covenant God has established in marriage.
Listen attentively to godly wisdom and instruction to navigate life’s moral challenges with discretion.
Remember that God sees all your actions and holds you accountable, motivating a life of holiness and obedience.
Repent promptly when you recognize sin in your life to avoid the destructive consequences described in this chapter.
conclusion: Proverbs Chapter 5 remains a timeless and sobering call to wisdom, urging believers to avoid the deadly snares of adultery and to embrace the joy and blessing of marital faithfulness. It underscores the importance of heeding godly instruction, recognizing God’s vigilant oversight, and understanding the grave consequences of sin. For the Christian today, this chapter reinforces the call to live with integrity, pursue holiness, and find satisfaction in the covenantal love God has ordained within marriage.

A bitter herb used metaphorically to describe the bitterness and unpleasant consequences of sin.
A double-edged sword symbolizing sharp, penetrating judgment or consequences that cut deeply.
A source of water, here symbolizing one’s marital relationship and sexual purity.
Godly teaching and correction intended to guide one in wisdom and righteous living.

outline.heading: The Seductive Danger of the Strange Woman
outline.description: The father warns the son about the deceptive allure of the adulterous woman whose sweetness conceals bitter destruction.

outline.heading: The Call to Avoid and the Consequences of Folly
outline.description: An urgent exhortation to keep away from temptation, with vivid warnings about the loss and regret that follow ignoring wisdom.

outline.heading: The Blessing of Marital Faithfulness
outline.description: A positive appeal to find joy and satisfaction exclusively in one’s spouse, celebrating the beauty of covenant love.

outline.heading: God’s Oversight and the Fate of the Wicked
outline.description: Affirms that God watches all human actions and that sin ultimately ensnares and destroys the unrepentant.
